sentences.text: The Insurance Company has preferred MFA No.32055/2013 against the judgment and award dated 20.05.2013 passed by the Prl. Senior Civil Judge & MACT, Gulbarga (hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal' for brevity) in MVC No.786/2012.

sentences.text: This appeal is premised on the ground of exorbitant compensation awarded to the claimant contrary to the material evidence placed on record and to set aside the judgment and award.

2. The claimant has preferred MFA No.201946/2014 against the same judgment and award, stated supra, on the ground of inadequate and meager compensation awarded by the Tribunal and seeks for enhancement of compensation.
3. Parties to the appeals shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

4. Brief facts of the case is as under:
On 24.10.2011 at about 02.00pm while the minor claimant Umme Kauser after attending her Diploma Classes at K.C.T. College, Gulbarga was returning to her house Umme Kausar S/O Maheboob Aalam Khazi vs Abdul Razak S/O Rukmuddin And Anr on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35282691/

sentences.text: situated at Taj Nagar, Muslim Sangha, Gulbarga by walk on the left side of the Road and when she approached Anwar Collge near Muslim Sangha, on Gulbarga - Aland Road, at that time an Autorickshaw bearing Registration No. KA-32 A-9977 came in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed her, due to the said impact she fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

5. The claimant was immediately shifted to KBN General Hospital, Gulbarga and thereafter to Tippu Sultan Hospital, Gulbarga and then to BTG Hospital, Gulbarga, where she took treatment as an inpatient from 24.10.2011 to 28.10.2011.
She was again admitted to Hospital as an inpatient from 28.10.2011 to 14.11.2011.
Due to the occurrence of accident, the claimant expended huge amount towards medical and incidental expenses.
6. The claimant was aged 17 years at the time of accident.
She was hale and healthy.
She was a student studying in Diploma at KCT Polytechnic, Gulbarga and also providing tuition classes and earning Rs.6,000/- per month.
The entire income of the claimant was used for her family maintenance.
Due to the said accident and injuries suffered, the claimant is not in position to do her work as she was doing prior to the accident and she is unable to get back to work.
Hence, she filed a claim petition before the Tribunal seeking compensation.
7. Respondents, respondent No.1 - Owner & Driver of the offending vehicle - Autorickshaw and respondent No.2 - Insurance Company appeared and filed their objections.

8. Respondent No.1 - Owner of the offending vehicle - Autorickshaw pleaded that the claim made by the claimant is exorbitant and denied the age, avocation and income including the injuries as alleged in the claim petition.
He further pleaded that he was holding the valid and effective Driving Licence as on the date of accident and the Autorickshaw was insured with respondent No.2 and the policy was in force.
He further states that that the claimant was on her wrong side, suddenly came to the center of the road and hit the offending vehicle.

Respondent No.1 pleaded that there was no negligence on his part and that if the liability is fastened by this Court against him the same would have to be indemnified by respondent No.2-insurer as respondent No.1 had insured his vehicle with respondent No.2.
On these grounds he sought for dismissal of claim petition.

9. The respondent No.2 - Insurance Company filed its detailed written statement contending that the claim made by the claimant in the claim petition is exorbitant and denied the age, avocation and income including the injuries as alleged in the claim petition.
He further contends that no such road traffic accident has occurred as alleged by the claimant.

It is further pleaded that claimant colluded with respondent No.1 in foisting a false and frivolous case only with an intention to make illegal gains, since in the FIR or complaint the vehicle details are not mentioned.
It is further pleaded by respondent No.2 that the claimant has not suffered any injuries as alleged in the claim petition.
On these grounds sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
10. On the basis of pleadings, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.

sentences.text:
In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, claimant got examined her father,
who is her Guardian since she is a minor, as PW1 and the Doctor as PW2 and got marked documents as Ex. P1 to P17, whereas respondents, in support of their case got examined PSI, Gulbarga as RW1 and Administrative Officer of respondent No.2 - Insurance Company as RW2 and got marked Ex.R1 - copy of the insurance policy.

12. The Tribunal based on the material evidence both oral and documentary produced before it,
awarded compensation of Rs.2,73,600/- with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation and directed the respondent No.2-Insurance Company to pay the compensation.
13. Being aggrieved by the meager compensation amount awarded, the claimant is before this Court in MFA No.201946/2014 seeking enhancement of compensation.
The Insurance Company has preferred MFA No.32055/2013 to set aside the impugned judgment and award.

14. The vehement contention of learned counsel for claimant is that the Tribunal has grossly erred in awarding meager compensation and has not taken into consideration the material evidence both oral and documentary thereby causing miscarriage of justice to the claimant.
He further contends that the Tribunal has not taken into consideration that the claimant is providing tuition classes and earning Rs.6,000/- per month other than prosecuting her studies in Diploma.
The Tribunal has assessed meager amount as income thereby committing an error in not awarding just and reasonable compensation.

Learned Counsel for claimant further contends that the Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income to be Rs.4,000/- per month whereas the Tribunal ought to have taken the income of the claimant at Rs.6,000/- per month.
15 . He further contends that though claimant has got adduced the evidence of PW2 - Doctor, who on oath stated and opined that the claimant has sustained fracture of shaft of right femur.
He also issued disability certificate at Ex.P6, which clearly discloses that claimant has suffered 17% disability to the whole body.
The claimant was fixed with rod and screws in situ of third shaft of right femur.

The Tribunal has taken the disability at 15% to the whole body, which is erroneous and same calls for interference.
16.

It is further contended that the Tribunal has awarded less compensation under the head loss of amenities, loss of income during laid-up period and also no amount is awarded for future medical expenses.
He further contends that even under the other heads the Tribunal has not awarded reasonable compensation commensurate to the injuries sustained by the claimant.
On the basis of these submissions, he seeks to allow the appeal and to enhance the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

17. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company vehemently contends that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is erroneous as it has not considered the material evidence both oral and documentary.

He further contends that the Tribunal has awarded exorbitant compensation based on the injuries sustained by the injured and interference by this Court is warranted under the facts and circumstances of the case.
He also contends that no cogent material evidence is placed on record to believe the statement now canvassed before this Court.

Therefore, on Umme Kausar S/O Maheboob Aalam Khazi vs Abdul Razak S/O Rukmuddin And Anr on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35282691/
5 the basis of these submissions, he seeks to dismiss the appeal as the same does not merit consideration and consequently allow the appeal preferred by the Insurance Company.

18. Having heard the learned counsel for the claimant and learned counsel for respondents, the points that would arise for consideration before this Court are:
i) Whether the claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation?
ii) Whether Insurance Company has made out a case for interference?
iii) What order ?
19. Having perused the entire material evidence both oral and documentary and the impugned judgment and award and having heard the submissions of learned counsel,
I am of the opinion that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding meager compensation thereby indulgence is called for in this case for enhancement of compensation.
No case is made out by the Insurance Company for interference.

20. It is not in dispute that the accident occurred on 24.10.2011 at about 02.00pm while the minor claimant Umme Kauser after attending her Diploma Classes at K.C.T. College, Gulbarga was returning to her house situated at Taj Nagar, Muslim Sangha, Gulbarga by walk on the left side of the Road and when she approached Anwar Collge near Muslim Sangha, on Gulbarga - Aland Road, at that time an Autorickshaw bearing Registration No. KA-32 A-9977 came in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed her, due to which both fell down and sustained grievous fracture injuries.
21.
The involvement of the vehicle, occurrence of accident, injuries having been sustained by the injured are all not disputed.
It is also not disputed that a case came to be registered with Rural Police Station, Gulbarga.
In order to substantiate this aspect and to prove the same the claimant has produced the documents as Exs.P1 to P5, which are the police records.
There is no challenge made by the driver or owner of the offending vehicle.

It is also not the case of respondent-Insurance Company that the said initiation of criminal proceedings is fictitious and concocted, so also, no contra material has been placed before the Tribunal or before this Court to prove the same as invalid or not being genuine.

But, the respondent No.1 - Owner cum Driver of the offending vehicle - Autorickshaw pleaded guilty before the V Addl. JMFC Court, Gulbarga in CC No.102/2012.
22.

Now, coming to the aspect of age, avocation and income of injured, no doubt the claimant has averred that she was aged about 17 years, a student studying in Diploma at KCT Polytechnic,
Gulbarga and she is also providing tuition and earning Rs.6,000/- per month, but however the fact Umme Kausar S/O Maheboob Aalam Khazi vs Abdul Razak S/O Rukmuddin And Anr on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35282691/
6 remains no documentary proof has been produced by the claimant with regard to her proof of income and no witnesses are examined to support her case and nothing material has been placed before the Court to substantiate the statement in proof of income.

sentences.text: In the absence of any cogent material proof of income, the Tribunal as well as this Court would have to do a guess work to assess the income.
In order to arrive at standard guess work, the Legal Services Authority has prescribed notional income chart, which prescribes Rs.6,000/- per month as income for accident of the year 2011.
The Tribunal has taken the income of the claimant at Rs.4,000/- per month for calculation of compensation towards loss of future earning on the basis of disability.
Accordingly, income requires to be assessed at Rs.6,000/- per month in the present case.

23. The injuries sustained by the claimant is described in the wound certificate at Ex.P6 and disability certificate at Ex.P12 issued by the Doctor, who has been examined as PW2, on the basis of the clinical analyses and assessment has given disability at 17% to the whole body.
The Tribunal has rightly assessed the disability at 15%, which requires no interference by this Court, which is just and reasonable under the facts and circumstances of the case.

24. The claimant was aged 17 years at the time of accident and proper multiplier to be adopted in the present case is '18' which is rightly adopted by the Tribunal and same does not call for interference.

Therefore, loss of future earning capacity due to permanent disability to the claimant would be Rs.1,94,400/- (Rs.6,000x12x18X15%) and same is awarded under this head as against a sum of Rs.1,29,600/- awarded by the Tribunal.
25. With regard to pain and suffering the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/-, which is just and proper and the same is retained.
26. Towards medical expenses and hospitalization charges the Tribunal is awarded a sum of Rs.70,000/- on the actual bills produced by the claimant, same is not interfered and is retained.

27. Towards attendant, nursing, extra nourishment charges and conveyance, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/-, which is on the lower side and I deem it appropriate to award a sum of Rs.15,000/- under this head.
28. Further, I am of the opinion that in view of the injuries suffered by the claimant towards loss of amenities the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/-.
There are fractures suffered by the claimant.
Therefore, an amount of Rs.30,000/- is required to be awarded and it is awarded under the head loss of amenities.
29. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.4,000/- under the head loss of income during laid up period.

This Court has taken the income of the claimant at Rs.6,000/- per month and claimant is required atleast three months period for recuperation, in view of injuries suffered by her and get into her day to day routine work.
Hence, the claimant would be entitled to compensation in a sum of Rs.18,000/- (Rs.6,000/- X 3) under this head.
